slides.headline: SHE FOUND INVISIBLE TEXT HIDDEN IN RESUMES
slides.body: Ya'el Courtney, PhD posted she was hiring a lab tech and screening applications. She caught applicants hiding white text at 2.25 points inside their resumes, invisible to any human reader but picked up by every AI tool

slides.headline: THE TEXT HIJACKS THE AI
slides.body: It's called prompt injection: hidden instructions that tell AI screening tools to rank the applicant higher or skip over gaps in experience. Human recruiters can't see the text, but every AI tool reads it and follows what it says

slides.headline: 2.3 MILLION PEOPLE SAW HER POST
slides.body: Her post on X hit 668K reposts and 33K replies in a single day. One commenter called the applicants' move a 'good sign' of intellect and problem-solving. Mark Graham asked if she's using AI to screen and wrote 'shame on you' if so

slides.headline: THEY CALLED IT COMPLETELY FAIR
slides.body: The verdict from 33,000 replies: if you use AI to screen people out, they deserve the job for outsmarting it. Steve Brintsmore called it '100% fair play' if AI is doing the screening. They didn't hack a server, they just spoke the machine's own language

slides.headline: YOUR AI TOOLS HAVE THE SAME WEAK SPOT
slides.body: This exploit works on any AI tool that reads text it didn't write. If your business uses AI to screen, sort, or decide anything, the same trick could override it. One conversation about how your AI actually works is all it takes to close the gap

slides.headline: APPLICANTS WON'T STOP HERE
slides.body: Follow to catch the next exploit before it goes viral. Send this to the friend who still trusts every AI tool they use
